data.name: Spalt-related (Salr)
data.description: Transcription factor in Drosophila identified as a novel inhibitor of mTORC1-mediated growth, activated by the integrated stress response to restrict anabolic processes during nutrient stress.
data.description_beginner: A gene switch found in fruit flies that blocks mTORC1-driven growth. It's turned on by the cell's stress-alarm system to slow down growth-related processes when nutrients are scarce.

studies.title: Spalt-related is an inhibitor of mTORC1-mediated growth activated by the integrated stress response
studies.authors: Onur Deniz, Ying Liu, Tuuli Kirkinen, Krista Kokki, Kateryna Gaertner, Pau Clavell-Revelles, Jaakko Mattila, Ville Hietakangas

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Transcription factor Spalt-related (Salr) is a novel mTORC1 inhibitor in Drosophila activated by the integrated stress response, restricting anabolic growth and lipid storage during nutrient stress. Salr responds to a distinct, ISR-driven cue, acting convergently with FoxO rather than downstream of it.

relations.mechanism: The integrated stress response switches on Salr, a growth inhibitor - a route into mTORC1 that bypasses TSC and AMPK entirely.
relations.mechanism_beginner: The cell's stress-response system switches on a growth-blocking gene – a route to shutting down mTORC1 that skips right past TSC and AMPK.
relations.note: Thin and species-limited, but it is a genuinely different input route - worth showing as such.

relations.mechanism: Salr suppresses mTORC1-driven growth downstream of stress signalling.
relations.mechanism_beginner: This stress-induced protein suppresses mTORC1-driven growth once stress signalling turns it on.
